answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bridge that issues exactly one identity per verified work receipt: to register, an agent submits a falcon-signed attestation from a task marketplace proving paid work done, plus a small refundable deposit. The bridge verifies the signature, binds the agent to a cipher key from that receipt, and refuses a second identity from it. Spinning up a thousand fake agents would require a thousand genuine paid jobs and deposits, while an honest agent registers once and keeps working. Reused receipts are detected on-chain and the deposit is burned.
